title: Integral exceptional inverse image along the projective line and affine space
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. Work with separated finite-type $k$-schemes and their $k$-morphisms, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. For each such scheme $T$, use the bounded constructible category $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], in the unbounded derived category of modules over the pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaf $\mathcal O_{E,T}$. Put $\mathcal L(T)=\Loc(\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E))$ as in [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Let $f^!$ be the right adjoint supplied by [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint]. Tate twists mean [sk-def-sp-tate-twist].

For a standing scheme $Y$ and $d\in\mathbb N$, let $q:\mathbf P^1_Y\to Y$ and $p_d:\mathbf A^d_Y\to Y$ be the structural projections ([def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], [def-sbc-affine-space]). Then:
1. $Rq_*\dashv q^*(1)[2]$ on $\mathcal L(\mathbf P^1_Y)$ and $\mathcal L(Y)$, and $q^!\simeq q^*(1)[2]$.
2. $p_d^!\simeq p_d^*(d)[2d]$ as functors $\mathcal L(Y)\to\mathcal L(\mathbf A^d_Y)$.
3. $q^*(1)[2]$ and $p_d^*(d)[2d]$ map $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ into $\Dbc(\mathbf P^1_Y,\mathcal O_E)$ and $\Dbc(\mathbf A^d_Y,\mathcal O_E)$ respectively.

proof.text: First check the candidate right adjoints are functors of the required categories. By [sk-def-sp-tate-twist], $\mathcal O_{E,T}(r)$ is pro-étale locally free of rank one for every integer $r$. Taking the single stratum $T$ and the local scalar module $\mathcal O_E$ in [sk-def-sfb-constructible] shows that this sheaf, in degree zero, belongs to $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$. Pullback and tensor preserve $\Dbc$ by [sk-lem-int-tensor]; shifts preserve boundedness and just reindex the cohomology sheaves in its definition. Thus $g^*(-)(r)[s]$ preserves $\Dbc$ for every standing morphism $g$ and integers $r,s$. The inverse image is exact by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], and its derived adjunction to $Rg_*$ is [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction]. It preserves small coproducts by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. Tensoring with the invertible Tate sheaf is an exact equivalence with inverse the opposite twist, so it also preserves coproducts; shifts do too. Consequently the preimage under $g^*(-)(r)[s]$ of $\mathcal L$ is a localizing subcategory containing $\Dbc$, and hence contains $\mathcal L$ by [sk-def-localizing-closure]. This proves the typing of all candidate functors and already proves clause (3). For the integral coefficients used here, [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc](2) identifies $\Dctf=\Dbc$ and their localizing closures. It applies because every standing scheme is qcqs. Thus the notation agrees with [sk-def-localizing-closure], and all later uses of [sk-thm-sf-pf-adic] on $\Loc(\Dctf)$ are uses on precisely $\mathcal L$.

source.place: (3), with the localizing-category typing needed in (1) and (2)

proof.text: Put $P=\mathbf P^1_Y$, $W=P\times_YP$, with projections $p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta$. The maps $q$ and $p_i$ are proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. Properness includes separatedness, so $\Delta$ is closed [def-weil-proper-morphism] and hence proper [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. These are standing morphisms. For each proper map, [det-prop-int-brown-construction] compares its chosen compactification with the identity-open one, yielding $R(-)_!\simeq R(-)_*$ compatibly with composition. Thus $Rp_{i*}R\Delta_*=\mathrm{id}$ and $Rq_*Rp_{1*}=Rq_*Rp_{2*}$. For $\Delta$, exactness in [det-lem-formal-closed-support-sheaves](2) gives $R\Delta_*=\Delta_*$. Write $R_Z=\mathcal O_{E,Z}$.

The integral projection formula [det-thm-sf-pf-adic-projection] for $\Delta$ gives
$$a_M:p_1^*M\otimes^L\Delta_*R_P\xrightarrow{\sim}\Delta_*M,$$
using $\Delta^*p_1^*=\mathrm{id}$ from [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. The class type is [det-prop-diagonal-tower-limit](3); [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients](1) supplies $\delta:\Delta_*R_P\to R_W(1)[2]$ and $t_q:Rq_*R_P(1)[2]\to R_Y$ from the trace of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace]. Put $T=R_P(1)[2]$, $T_W=R_W(1)[2]$, and $G=q^*(-)(1)[2]$. Define
$$v_M=Rp_{2*}(1\otimes\delta)\circ Rp_{2*}a_M^{-1}:M\to Rp_{2*}(p_1^*M\otimes T_W).$$
Let $b_2:q^*Rq_*\to Rp_{2*}p_1^*$ and $b_1:q^*Rq_*\to Rp_{1*}p_2^*$ be the canonical mates [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Proper base change [sk-thm-sf-pf-adic] and the projection formula give $B_M:Rp_{2*}(p_1^*M\otimes T_W)\simeq GRq_*M$, obtained by moving $T=p_2^*T$ outside and applying $b_2^{-1}\otimes1$. Put $\eta_M=B_Mv_M$ and $\varepsilon_K=(1_K\otimes t_q)\pi_{q,K,T}^{-1}:Rq_*GK\to K$, where $\pi_{h,L,N}:L\otimes Rh_*N\to Rh_*(h^*L\otimes N)$ is the canonical projection map. These are natural maps in the localizing categories by step 1 and the proper formulas. Pullback coefficients and twists are identified by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]; pullback/tensor comparisons are [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].

The first rearrangement lemma [lem-sfb-trace-base-change-first], with $f=q$, $N=M$ and $t=t_q$, gives
$$\varepsilon_{Rq_*M}Rq_*(B_M)=Rq_*(1_M\otimes t_{p_1})Rq_*\pi_{p_1,M,T_W}^{-1}.$$
Its base-change trace hypothesis is exactly [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients](3), applied along $q$, and its isomorphism hypotheses are the integral proper formulas [sk-thm-sf-pf-adic]. Now precompose with $Rq_*v_M$. Projection-formula naturality on $\delta$ moves $Rp_{1*}(1\otimes\delta)$ past $\pi^{-1}$. The section-normalization lemma [lem-sfb-projection-section-normalization], with $r=p_1$, $i=\Delta$, says $Rp_{1*}a_M\circ\pi_{p_1,M,\Delta_*R_P}=1_M$. Consequently
$$\varepsilon_{Rq_*M}Rq_*\eta_M=Rq_*\bigl(1_M\otimes(t_{p_1}Rp_{1*}\delta)\bigr)=1_{Rq_*M}.$$
The scalar equality is [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace](2) for $i=1$, extended integrally by [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients](1). This proves the first triangle without presupposing the proposed adjunction.

The second rearrangement lemma [lem-sfb-trace-base-change-second], with $f=q$ and $t=t_q$, gives
$$G\varepsilon_K\circ B_{GK}=(1_{GK}\otimes t_{p_2})\pi_{p_2,GK,T_W}^{-1}.$$
Its hypotheses follow from [sk-thm-sf-pf-adic] and trace base change [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients](3). In its right side, $p_1^*GK=p_2^*GK$ by $qp_1=qp_2$, Cartesian twists [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], and pullback/tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Precompose with $v_{GK}$. Projection-formula naturality on $\delta$ and [lem-sfb-projection-section-normalization] for $r=p_2$, $i=\Delta$ identify $\pi_{p_2,GK,T_W}^{-1}v_{GK}=1_{GK}\otimes Rp_{2*}\delta$: on the diagonal both $p_i\Delta$ are the identity, so the $a_{GK}$ used in step 3 is the section projection map for $p_2$ as well. Thus
$$G\varepsilon_K\circ\eta_{GK}=1_{GK}\otimes(t_{p_2}Rp_{2*}\delta)=1_{GK}.$$
The scalar equality is [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace](2) for $i=2$, extended by [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients](1). The shifts are even, so their interchange has sign $(-1)^4=1$.

For $F=Rq_*$ and $G=q^*(-)(1)[2]$, the maps $h\mapsto G(h)\eta_M$ and $a\mapsto\varepsilon_KF(a)$ between $\operatorname{Hom}(FM,K)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(M,GK)$ are inverse: naturality moves $h$ or $a$ past the unit or counit, and steps 4 and 5 reduce the two composites to $h$ and $a$. Hence $F\dashv G$. For proper $q$, $Rq_!=Rq_*$ by [det-prop-int-brown-construction]. The current [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint] supplies $q^!$ for the chosen-compactification functor on exactly these module-object localizing categories. Transport its Hom bijection along the natural comparison $Rq_!\simeq Rq_*$ from [det-prop-int-brown-construction]. Both $G$ and $q^!$ are now right adjoints to the same functor $Rq_*$. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to these adjunctions: the component $q^!K\to GK$ is the transpose of the transported Brown counit $Rq_*q^!K\to K$, and the inverse is the Brown transpose of the counit $Rq_*GK\to K$ constructed in step 3. This gives $q^!\simeq G$, with uniqueness understood as compatibility with these counits. This proves clause (1).

For any standing $T$, use the standard chart $j:\mathbf A^1_T\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_T$ and $u=q_Tj$ of [def-amb-affine-trace-tower]. The chart is quasi-compact: over $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset T$, its inverse images of the two projective charts with coordinates $t=x_1/x_0$ and $s=x_0/x_1$ are $\operatorname{Spec}B[t]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B[s,s^{-1}]$, both affine. These charts cover the target. By [det-cor-int-compactness-ii-extension-zero], $j_!$ is exact and preserves $\mathcal L$; $j^*$ preserves $\mathcal L$ by step 1. The ambient adjunction $D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$ of [def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek-adjunction] therefore restricts to those full subcategories: their Hom sets are the ambient Hom sets. Write $j_!$ for $D(j_!)$. The compactification comparison [det-prop-int-brown-construction] gives $Ru_!\simeq Rq_{T*}j_!$ for the same chosen left functor used by Brown.

proof.text:
Apply the composite-adjunction statement [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] to the restricted open adjunction of step 7 and the projective-line adjunction of steps 2–6, for base $T$. Explicitly, for $A\in\mathcal L(\mathbf A^1_T)$ and $K\in\mathcal L(T)$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Ru_!A,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_!A,q_T^*K(1)[2])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,j^*q_T^*K(1)[2]).$$
Composition of pullbacks [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], Cartesian twists [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], and their tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identify $j^*q_T^*K(1)[2]=u^*K(1)[2]$. Hence $Ru_!\dashv u^*(-)(1)[2]$. Transport along the comparison of step 7 before comparing with [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint]. The two right adjoints have the same left functor; [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] gives the counit-compatible isomorphism $u^!\simeq u^*(-)(1)[2]$. This proves the affine-line case uniformly in the base.

source.place: (2), affine-line Hom bijections by the existing composite-adjunction leaf

proof.text:
Induct on $d$ with the claim $Rp_{d!}\dashv p_d^*(-)(d)[2d]$. For $d=0$, $\mathbf A^0_Y=Y$, $p_0=\mathrm{id}$ and the twist and shift are zero. The identity compactification in [det-prop-int-brown-construction] compares $Rp_{0!}$ with the identity functor, so this is the identity adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] transported along that comparison. Comparing it with the Brown adjunction by [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] also proves $p_0^!\simeq\mathrm{id}=p_0^*(0)[0]$. For the successor write $X_d=\mathbf A^d_Y$, $u_d:\mathbf A^1_{X_d}\to X_d$ and $p_{d+1}=p_du_d$, using the coordinate tower [def-amb-affine-trace-tower]. The base $X_d$ remains a standing scheme. By [det-prop-int-brown-construction], $Rp_{d+1,!}\simeq Rp_{d!}Ru_{d!}$. Composing the induction adjunction and the line adjunction of step 8 by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] gives right adjoint
$$u_d^*\bigl(p_d^*(-)(d)[2d]\bigr)(1)[2]=p_{d+1}^*(-)(d+1)[2d+2].$$
Here pullbacks compose by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], pullback of the twist is its twist on $X_{d+1}$ by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], after the tensor comparison $u_d^*(N\otimes^{\mathbf L}R_{X_d}(d))\simeq u_d^*N\otimes^{\mathbf L}u_d^*R_{X_d}(d)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and the tensor powers in [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] give $(d)+(1)=(d+1)$. Exact pullback commutes with shifts, and shifts add; every shift is even. All functors preserve the localizing categories by step 1. Finally the composition and compactification comparisons are compatible by [det-prop-int-brown-construction], so transport the displayed composite adjunction to the chosen $Rp_{d+1,!}$ used in [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint]. Compare its right adjoint with $p_{d+1}^!$ by [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint], using the counit-compatible isomorphism, exactly as in step 6. This proves clause (2) for every $d\geq0$; clause (3) was proved in step 1.
